task.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H4): Token-stationary one-launch FP16x3 tcgen05 kernel, fp32 h in TMEM, per-batch counters, for N <= 18944 (S+M rows). 1) Start from the #129 lineage-M engine (read_example solx_129_token_stationary_tcgen05.cu): SW128 descriptors, kind::f16 idesc, elect.sync issue, release/acquire counters with departure reset, gelu2, cooperative launch at 1 CTA/SM, 512 threads. 2) Tokens per CTA t = ceil16(N/148) capped at 96 (12544 tokens -> 96 x 131 CTAs; 6272 -> 48; 3136 -> 32; 784/1568 -> 16). A CTA's tokens may straddle 2 batches (HW=196): keep two batch slots as in #129. 3) Phase 0: every CTA converts 1/G of W1 and W2 into exact fp16 hi/lo SW128 images in a torch.empty workspace, computes part of b2' = b2 + W2.gb, then bumps one counter. The x tile lands by bulk copy and is split hi/lo in registers into the B tile. 4) GEMM1 swap-AB D1[hidden 128-block][t]: 4 blocks, with the 3 products as K-concatenated passes; W1 hi/lo streamed in 64 KB blocks through a 2-stage ring. Epilogue: + b1, gelu2, per-channel sumsq, fp32 h back into TMEM with tcgen05.st, red.add into gsum[b][512], per-batch counter. 5) After the batch wait: s_b = 1 + gw*G/(mean G + eps) with exact sqrt and div; h' = h*s_b split hi/lo into smem per 128-k chunk; GEMM2 D2[out 128][t] with hi*hi in one accumulator and the cross terms in a second one placed in freed h columns (TMEM <= 512); W2 hi/lo streamed per 64 KB k-chunk. out = A + B + b2', stored coalesced [token][128] with evict_last. 6) Rows with N > 18944 route to the r0-simt-3k path unchanged. One launch per call; torch.empty is the only torch call in run(). 7) Add %globaltimer phase stamps (weights ready, x landed, GEMM1, epilogue, batch wait, GEMM2, store) at 1,28,28, 4,28,28, 2,56,56, 4,56,56 and 16,28,28, and a SASS count of epilogue instructions per element. 8) run_tests all 14 rows; log err/tol per row over 10 rounds. If the 12544-token rows miss the gate, measure the fallback configuration t = 64 with more CTAs (2 rounds) and ship the better one. Success: All 9 rows with N <= 18944 pass with err/tol <= 0.8; 12544-token rows <= 21 us rented, 6272 <= 15 us, 784 <= 13 us. Refuted if: After the fallback configuration the 12544-token rows exceed 30 us rented, and the stamps show weight landing plus batch wait above 50% of the kernel time (a structural cost, not a bug). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). A missed gate or success line is not a reason to stop: switch to the best configuration your own probes found (or the experiment's next variant), build it into a full kernel and measure it with run_tests, and use the rest of the budget on it. Hand in a measured kernel that implements this experiment's design on at least one workload (others may fall back); the r0 baseline or the unchanged parent is not a valid candidate unless a measured hardware fact rules the design out (name it, with the probe's number). Record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Keep the kernel copy-like (memory-bound): the portal locks the SM clock lower than the test bench and penalises extra SM work per byte (the problem card). Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); any h ring or scratch is reused only within one call, never across calls; grid, cluster or per-batch counters live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only (tcgen05 does not build for LOCAL); TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted or split weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value; cache hints only on our own workspace buffers, never on hidden_states, the weights or the output; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build; 10-round fp64 precision log on every shipped row (err/tol).
